title: Refactor presubmit runner: modular test harness, fast-smoke preflight, and dependency upgrades
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Introduce modular presubmit runner with a lightweight fast-smoke preflight lane; upgrade protobuf & build-image toolchain; reduce CI image size and accelerate feedback. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic presubmit runner has grown slow and brittle. Developers waiting for feedback spend time context-switching; infra costs are higher than necessary. This PR splits the presubmit harness into per-package modular runners, adds a small fast-smoke preflight lane that runs in ~30s for quick feedback, and upgrades a few build deps to unlock smaller build images.

What this does (summary):
- Introduce tools/presubmit/runner package responsible for dispatching tests per package and collecting results.
- Add ci/presubmit/fast-smoke workflow that runs a curated subset of tests (lint + critical smoke + lightweight integration stubs).
- Shrink docker/build-image to a slim variant and move build-toolchain installation into layered cache steps. Image size reduced ~230MB.
- Upgrade protobuf to 3.21.9 and bump protoc-gen-go to v1.30.0 to fix generated code warnings in ENG-2390.
- Replace legacy monorepo jest-mocha runner with an adapter that invokes per-package harness commands; preserves existing test contracts.
- Add a preflight safety check action (ci/actions/preflight-safety) that validates release artifacts and lockfile drift before any release job.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc posted in Linear (ENG-2345) with benchmarks
- [x] Unit + integration tests for runner logic
- [x] Migration shims to avoid breaking older release lanes
- [x] CI workflows added and smoke-lane gated behind feature flag

Design notes: The presubmit runner exposes a small JSON contract (package, tags, parallelism). The orchestrator schedules package-level runs such that packages with fast tests are favored for the fast-smoke lane. The full presubmit remains available for full CI. The migration is staged: the fast-smoke lane is opt-in for teams via a repo-level label until we hit 30% adoption.

Testing & rollout:
- Ran the new fast-smoke lane against the redwood monorepo and recorded median feedback time drop from ~4:20 to ~0:38 for target changes.
- Performed dogfood runs on redwood-examples (branch: ci-dogfood/presubmit) for two weeks.
- Staged rollout: enabled default for repo contributors on 2026-03-01 after one approver signoff.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: missed fragile tests by fast-smoke. Mitigation: curated test list with opt-out labels and automatic fallback to full presubmit on failure.
- Risk: toolchain upgrade may change generated proto behavior. Mitigation: vendored generated code diffed and small fixes applied in this PR.

Related: ENG-2345, ENG-2390, SUP-54321.

Documentation: Updated docs/presubmit.md with new runner CLI and config examples. Updated release runbook to include preflight-safety step.
